newsitem.title: USA: Judge dismisses charges against Henry Espy.
newsitem.headline: Judge dismisses charges against Henry Espy.

text.p: A U.S. District Court in Oxford, Mississippi, Tuesday dismissed remaining fraud-related charges against Henry Espy, the brother of former Clinton cabinet member Mike Espy.
Donald Smaltz, the independent counsel heading the probe into Mike Espy, announced the outcome in a statement released here.
"We accept the judge's decision and move forward," Smaltz said.

The indictment charged Henry Espy with one count of conspiracy to defraud and five counts of making false statements to the First National Bank of Clarksdale in connection with a $75,000 campaign loan.
Alvarez Ferrouillet, a New Orleans lawyer, pleaded guilty to the same idictment Feb. 24.
The loan was to repay debts accumulated during Henry Espy's unsuccessful campaign to obtain the congressional seat vacated by his brother when Mike Espy became agriculture secretary.
Mike Espy resigned from the cabinet in 1994 because of allegations he accepted illegal gifts and favours from firms his department was responsible for regulating.
The investigation of Mike Espy is continuing, Smaltz said. No charges have been brought against him.
